newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed slightly lower on Friday, a move which could signal the start of a period of profit-taking after the index's steady rise this year, brokers said.

The all share index closed 0.43 points down at 636.79. Price gains led declines by 19 to 13. Blue chips Commercial Bank Ltd fell three rupees to 155, Development Finance Corporation of Ceylon Ltd five rupees to 265.
"Since the index has risen steadily since January, there is profit-taking setting in," said Shafi Waheed, a trader at CDIC Sasoon Cumberbatch.
The all share index has risen 30.09 points so far this year.

"We have begun to take between five to seven percent profits in a number of growth stocks among conglomerates, finance and manufacturing sector shares," said Derendra Abayaratna, fund manger at Century Growth Fund.
Turnover was 60.43 million rupees on 2.18 million shares, led by 117,100 Aitken Spence & C0, 341,700 Distilleries Co of Sri Lanka Ltd, 429,900 Ceylon Grain Elevators Ltd and 113,400 Haycarb Ltd.
But brokers did not expect the index to fall sharply due to buying interest generated by good 1996 profits.
